Introduction
To better reflect our evolving research strengths and foster specialised academic growth, the Department of Applied Biology and Chemical Technology (ABCT) has been restructured into two new departments—the Department of Chemistry (CHEM) and the Department of Life Sciences (LS) from 1 July 2026. Building on the strong foundation of ABCT, CHEM embarks on an exciting new chapter at the forefront of scientific discovery and innovation.
Driven by the global mandate for sustainability, CHEM channels its cutting-edge research capacity into six strategic pillars: Advanced Nanomaterials, AI-driven Green Chemistry and Catalysis, Macromolecular Sciences, Chemical Sensors and Imaging, Energy Storage and Conversion Technologies, and Photonic and Optoelectronic Materials. Our dynamic and expanding portfolio seamlessly bridges fundamental chemistry with real-world applications.
Please visit our website for more information about our research areas and programmes.
Research Area
Chemistry
Chemical research in the department is led by academics covering a wide spectrum of areas, divided into the categories listed below. The Department is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities to support interdisciplinary collaborations and high-level research on topics from fundamental concepts to practical applications.

Supporting Documents
Academic Referee's Report
Compulsory - Two Academic Referee's Reports are required for all fellowship and scholarship applicants.
Identify and invite two academics who are familiar with your academic performance and achievements. Proposed supervisor(s) from the PolyU, proposed supervisor(s) from the partner institution (if any), and persons from non-academic backgrounds are not considered appropriate academic referees.
Provide complete and accurate information on your referees, including their email addresses under a university or an organisation, in your online application.
